B Bloodraven in Production Unit 4
Unit 4

Where failover meets your application

Bloodraven's job ends at a label selector and a DNS record; your application's job starts there. This unit closes the gap Unit 3 opened — the promotion that worked perfectly while the counter app carried on reading from the demoted site, with nothing paging. You will fix a connection pool, move a primary on purpose at an RPO of zero, and decide what your cache and sessions owe you. Everything so far has assumed somebody can see the truth about orders; Unit 5 removes that assumption.

Topics

Services, DNS steering, and taints
Connection pools that survive a promotion
Planned failover: moving the primary on purpose
Cache and sessions that follow the primary

Unit test

Quick check: can you say why a pooled connection keeps serving stale reads after a correct promotion, name the one path that actually drains connections, and read a sessionsPreserved of nil without guessing?

Take the unit test →

Project

Make the writer survive

Instrument a writer against orders, run both a planned and an emergency failover underneath it, and produce a drill record with the measured write-gap for each — so the recovery time you claim for your application is one you observed rather than one you assumed.
